speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Quantum gravity, higher-spin indices and superselfduality
summary: The actual new talk begins on P000841 and ends on P000842. Kallosh reports on the Cambridge relativity meeting, then describes higher-spin zero-mode formulae and self-dual supergravity. P000840 is a carry-in from the preceding notebook material: its vertex-model, Yang--Baxter and Ising observations were already indexed as 1978-460.12--20. They are preserved as provenance, not reassigned to Kallosh or duplicated as 1979 occurrences. The overlapping catalogue page interval is retained in the provenance crosswalk; the source-page field gives the actual talk span. The programme of a superspace index theorem is distinguished from the concrete index computations and from any claim of unrestricted ultraviolet finiteness.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Degenerate dispersion laws, resonances and integrability
summary: The talk begins on P000843, after Kallosh's report. Zakharov studies additional additive functions on wave-resonance manifolds, difference-curve parametrizations, dressing and a necessary resonance test for extra Hamiltonian integrals. Arnold connects this with translation surfaces, Poincaré obstructions and formal Birkhoff normal form. The subsequent programme appears in Zakharov--Schulman (1980, 1988) and the later Balk--Ferapontov web classification (1994); one additional collision invariant and infinitely many are distinct hypotheses. None of these statements identifies every notion of nonlinear integrability with degenerate scalar dispersion. P000847 ends with Gelfand's reading programme.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Spinors, quaternions and the Dirac equation
summary: P000848 contains Gelfand's introductory discussion of spinors, the projective action of two-component vectors, Hamilton's square-root idea and physical consequences of the Dirac theory. The quaternion conclusion requires an extra quotient relation: three anticommuting square roots of minus one alone generate a Clifford algebra. Kallosh's subsequent programme begins at the foot of the same page.

speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Spinor calculus and gravitational index theorems
summary: The eight-part programme on P000848 is followed on P000849--P000853 by two-spinor calculus, self-duality, Laplace-type operators, heat coefficients and higher-spin spectral pairings. The notes themselves correct a proposed interpretation of the nonzero-mode term as a common eigenvalue multiplicity. They also contain incompatible numerical versions of an index formula on P000841 and P000853; these are recorded without silently repairing an unverified normalization. The dated heading on P000854 starts the next meeting.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Reading programme and exercises
summary: The actual contribution is the opening of P000854: a reading programme and exercises on Gaussian and quartic Fourier integrals and on self-adjoint operators for a symplectic form. The exercises are definite mathematical items, although the contribution is primarily a programme. Their solutions must distinguish the self-adjoint relation for an alternating form from the Hamiltonian, skew-adjoint relation.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Twistors and the conformal compactification of Minkowski space
summary: Starting on P000854, Gindikin describes the Hermitian space of signature (2,2), its two-plane Grassmannian, tube domains, the real Minkowski chart and null incidence. This continues the geometry of 1978-455.1. The manuscript's unrestricted affine chart stabilizer includes dilations, and its final point/ray correspondence interchanges the two sides of the twistor incidence relation. The higher-dimensional challenge is a programme, not a unique conjecture.

speaker: F. A. Berezin
title: Grassmann algebra, supermatrices and classification problems
summary: The dated lecture begins on P000859 and ends with two explicit matrix problems at the top of P000862. Gelfand proposes graph analogues of the even Grassmann algebra; Gindikin then recalls the BGG description of projective bundles and asks for actual maps and a Grassmannian counterpart. The repeated-body-spectrum problem is separated from the odd-entry commutant problem. Finite coefficient algorithms solve the literal finite-dimensional computational tasks; this chapter examines what additional structural information they provide.

speaker: G. B. Shabat
title: Double translation hypersurfaces and the Lie--Wirtinger theorem
summary: The contribution starts at the bottom of P000862 and ends midway down P000863. The catalogue names G. B. Shabat; the manuscript initial looks like \ru{Ю.}, a retained attribution discrepancy. The discussion explains the theta-divisor example and reports the classical converse, followed by Gelfand's broad integrability speculation. Genericity and the distinction between smooth Jacobians, generalized Jacobians and degenerations are indispensable.

speaker: Raphael Høegh-Krohn
title: Energy representations of current groups and Brownian paths
summary: The actual talk occupies the lower part of P000863 and P000864--P000865, translated by Gelfand. It constructs the energy representation, states irreducibility in dimension at least three, asks about dimension two and explains the one-dimensional Brownian realization. The name bears a question mark in the notebook but is identified by the catalogue. The construction needs a Gaussian realization outside the Hilbert space and a consistent Maurer--Cartan convention. A later claimed proof in every dimension cannot settle the two-dimensional question: the primary literature explicitly identifies a gap.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: First-class constraints and structure functions
summary: The dated block on P000866 introduces first-class constraints, asks whether their structure functions can be made constant, and writes a multiplier action. The catalogue attributes it to Batalin; the notebook's tentative \ru{Некто (Батурин)} is retained as an attribution uncertainty. The catalogue's overlapping P000864--P000867 interval is not a literal boundary: the new block starts on P000866 and ends before Kallosh's heading on that page.

speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Background-field quantization, ghosts and gauge dependence
summary: Kallosh relates formal generating functionals and scattering amplitudes, then presents background-field gauge fixing for gravity, ghost terms, and an on-shell gauge-independence argument. Maxwell theory supplies a transparent example of gauge degeneracy. Several formulas suppress normalization, loop order, or curvature terms. The supergravity discussion concerns gauge-algebra and ghost modifications; it does not claim ultraviolet finiteness.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Faddeev--Popov reduction and BRST invariance
summary: The scan on P000871 dates this lecture \ru{29/X-79}, so 29 October is used here; the supplied catalogue's 29 September is recorded as a provenance discrepancy. After stationary phase and Maxwell gauge degeneracy, a finite-dimensional group-action model derives the gauge-slice determinant and ghost representation. BRST transformations, physical unitarity, gauge independence, open supergravity algebras and the Yang--Mills example follow. The notes are an exposition of methods circulating before the talk, not an instance of the later odd-antibracket BV formalism.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Gravity, Einstein metrics and the gravitational boundary action
summary: The heading says \ru{По Хокингу}. Gelfand compares approaches to quantum gravity, writes the Einstein--Hilbert variational problem, mentions Yau, and motivates the gravitational boundary term and reference subtraction. The notebook's purported universal uniqueness theorem for Einstein metrics is substantially false. The corrected Kähler statements are identified with Yau's 1977 announcement/1978 proof; the boundary action matches Gibbons--Hawking 1977.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Graded constraints, Dirac brackets and phase-space measures
summary: The lecture develops graded canonical brackets, first- and second-class constraints, reduction by Dirac brackets, and the phase-space path integral. Gelfand recognizes the Dirac bracket as the inverse of the induced symplectic form. Source-generating equations lead to a formal constrained integral with the square-root Berezinian; adding gauge conditions makes a regular first-class system second class. These are pre-existing Hamiltonian methods, with a contemporaneous 1977/1978 graded extension.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dilogarithms and six proposed connections
summary: The dated introductory page asks where dilogarithms occur and lists six areas, then writes an integral and a differential five-term relation. The catalogue attributes this introduction to Gelfand, although the page itself says only Gelfand seminar. In the actual notebook it precedes Beilinson's P000885--P000886 contribution (record 476); the catalogue numbers reverse that order. The list is a research map, not six fully formulated conjectures.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Dilogarithms, tame symbols and regulators of curves
summary: Beilinson explains the real dilogarithmic regulator, its Steinberg identity and tame-symbol periods, then refines it to a complex multiplicative regulator. The latter matches his short 1980 publication closely. The opening remark about zeta functions has no sufficiently precise arithmetic conjecture. Source errors include the sign of the zeta(2) integral, a missing period normalization, and calling a multiplicative skew symbol symmetric. The distinction between K-theory of the curve and its function field is essential.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Hamiltonian BRST quantization in a relativistic gauge
summary: The second Batalin contribution on 19 November extends phase space by multiplier momenta and ghosts, introduces an odd nilpotent BRST charge and a gauge fermion, and sketches gauge independence by a field-dependent BRST change of variables. This is the contemporaneous Hamiltonian BFV framework, whose even Poisson bracket must be distinguished from the later BV antibracket. The statement about termination of supergravity ghost expansions remains model dependent.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Elementary particles, gauge representations and the Higgs potential
summary: The speaker is called physicist in this block and identified as Kobzarev by the catalogue and the following lecture's tentative name. The talk surveys quark and lepton charges, three generations, colour and chiral weak representations, gauge-boson exchange and a gauge-invariant scalar potential. It is exposition of pre-existing physics rather than a new theorem announcement. Its massless-neutrino language and unobserved top quark are retained as 1979 context, with current status distinguished.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Confinement heuristics and the electroweak mass mechanism
summary: The continuation first contrasts Coulomb fields with a proposed chromoelectric tube, with a short intervention attributed to Manin. It then derives the scalar Hessian, symmetry zero modes, gauge-boson masses, the Higgs-doublet breaking pattern, weak mixing, currents and fermion masses, ending with the quark mixing matrix. The confinement picture is distinguished from its still-open four-dimensional continuum formulation. The Higgs and weak-interaction material is principally exposition of older results, with explicit corrections to several notebook formulas.

title: The catalog heading YEAR 1980
summary: This undated catalog record is a year divider, not a separate mathematical session. The supplied page window overlaps Migdal: the first visible heading on P000900 is explicitly 21 January 1980. No mathematical item is duplicated under this heading.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Yang--Mills theory in loop space
summary: The actual notes occupy P000900--P000904; P000905 starts the next session. Migdal replaces a gauge potential by traces of parallel transport, defines area and path derivatives, and converts the classical Yang--Mills equation and formal Schwinger--Dyson identity to loop equations. Color contraction produces a multiloop hierarchy; normalized large-rank factorization formally closes it. The final assertion about confinement is a research aspiration, not a proof recorded in these pages. Gelfand intervenes on characters of the path group. The principal equation had already appeared in December 1979; the talk is not its first publication.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials and representations
summary: The notes actually continue through the upper part of P000907, before MacPherson begins. Zelevinsky explicitly discusses the 1979 paper of Kazhdan and Lusztig: Coxeter and Hecke algebra preliminaries, the bar-invariant basis, multiplication and cell representations. The Verma-module multiplicity formula and Vogan\textquotesingle s cohomological reformulations are distinguished as conjectures. Their later proofs must not be confused with the basis theorem already proved in 1979.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Intersection homology and Schubert singularities
summary: The actual contribution begins at the MacPherson heading in the lower part of P000907 and ends on that page. It introduces intersection homology, its smooth-space normalization and rational duality, and its interpretation of Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials. The question mark in the grading shift is preserved as incomplete notation. P000908 begins the 4 February session; it is not a continuation of the January intersection-homology talk. The notebook calls the speaker Bob; his name is Robert D. MacPherson.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Unitary representations of infinite classical groups
summary: The upper part of P000908 describes a multiparameter family for the infinite real general linear group, with finite-multiplicity discrete restriction to its orthogonal subgroup, and type-I/classification results for completed groups of fixed finite real rank. The completion topology and the distinction between the 1978 type-I theorem and the more complete 1980 construction are indispensable. MacPherson begins a separate contribution below the named heading on the same page.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Combinatorial Pontryagin classes and the dilogarithm
summary: The contribution begins below Olshanskii on P000908 and occupies P000908--P000913. Most of the construction is identifiable in MacPherson\textquotesingle s February 1977 Bourbaki exposition, published in 1978: locally linear stars, hypersimplices, configuration complexes, the compatible product complex and the signed \(1/48\) cocycle for \(p_1\). The end moves to Grassmannians and a dilogarithmic primitive, developed with Gelfand in their 1982 paper. The 11 February heading on P000914 begins the next talk. This is a return to the characteristic-class line in occurrences 1976-413.5--11, not a continuation of the January intersection-homology discussion.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Grassmannians, hypersimplices and enhanced configurations
summary: The actual source is the short, separately dated fragment P000914; P000915 starts Zakharov on 18 February. It states the idea that a Grassmannian point is determined by a hypersimplicial datum and an enhanced projective configuration, with \(n+k\) labelled vectors in a \(k\)-dimensional space. The projected-space dimension is written incorrectly, and the bottom of the fragment is clipped. The finite statement is already present in the 1977/1978 Bourbaki exposition; no missing continuation is invented.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Benney equations, conservation laws and Hamiltonian variables
summary: The actual session occupies P000915--P000916. Starting from an incompressible fluid with a free surface, Zakharov takes the hydrostatic long-wave approximation and announces additional conservation laws, simpler Hamiltonian variables, and an extension to two horizontal dimensions. Gelfand interprets the model as collective dynamics through a common field. The contemporary papers supply precise versions of the short announcements; no theorem of complete integrability is attributed to these notes. P000917 explicitly starts 22 September 1980, with Fuchs on intersection homology; P000918 continues that discussion and turns to Graev on integral geometry. Those next-year items are inventoried separately in \texttt{code/boundary\_inventory.md} and are not occurrences of this record.
